title: Cricket: coaching overview
d: Coaching Cricket means teaching score more runs than the opponent within formats: T20 (~3 hrs), ODI (~8 hrs), Test (up to 5 days).
definition: Coaching Cricket means teaching score more runs than the opponent within formats: T20 (~3 hrs), ODI (~8 hrs), Test (up to 5 days).
description: Coaching Cricket is teaching people to achieve the objective — score more runs than the opponent — inside the constraints of formats: T20 (~3 hrs), ODI (~8 hrs), Test (up to 5 days) and the laws of the game. The coach's job has four parts: design practices that build skill, manage people so they perform, make decisions under pressure, and develop athletes as people. This database covers all four, grounded in the real rules and demands of Cricket: 11 players per side.

title: Coaching philosophy
d: Great Cricket coaches are teachers first: clear, demanding, and consistent.
definition: Great Cricket coaches are teachers first: clear, demanding, and consistent.
description: A Cricket coaching philosophy answers three questions: how we play, how we treat people, and what winning means here. Write it down in one page and live it — athletes detect hypocrisy instantly. The best philosophies are simple enough for a twelve-year-old to repeat and strong enough to guide a championship: effort, respect, and the courage to keep learning.

title: Teaching key rule 1
d: Teach Cricket rule 1: Each innings ends after 10 wickets fall or the allotted overs are bowled..
definition: Teach Cricket rule 1: Each innings ends after 10 wickets fall or the allotted overs are bowled..
description: Teaching Cricket rule 1 — Each innings ends after 10 wickets fall or the allotted overs are bowled. — works best in three steps: explain the reason (the unfair advantage it prevents), demonstrate it live, then drill it under pressure until compliance is automatic. Test understanding with scenarios, not quizzes: freeze a practice and ask what the call should be. Athletes who understand the why rarely need reminding of the what.

title: Designing sessions
d: A Cricket session: warm-up, skill, tactical, conditioned game, cool-down.
definition: A Cricket session: warm-up, skill, tactical, conditioned game, cool-down.
description: Design Cricket sessions in five blocks: dynamic warm-up with the ball or implement, one skill focus, one tactical focus, a conditioned game that rewards the day's theme, and a cool-down with review. Plan 90 minutes and protect the plan — the loudest parent never outranks the session objective. Every drill answers: what will be better after this?

title: Giving feedback
d: Feedback in Cricket: one thing, specific, immediate, then a retry.
definition: Feedback in Cricket: one thing, specific, immediate, then a retry.
description: Feedback that changes Cricket performance is specific, immediate, and limited to one thing: name what you saw, name the fix, and give a retry within seconds. Sandwich praise around corrections at a 3-to-1 ratio for young athletes; elite athletes can take it straight. Never coach the mistake you just praised away — pick your moment.

title: Motivating athletes
d: Motivate Cricket players with autonomy, mastery, and belonging.
definition: Motivate Cricket players with autonomy, mastery, and belonging.
description: Motivation in Cricket lasts when it comes from inside: give athletes choices (autonomy), visible improvement (mastery), and a team worth belonging to. Carrots and sticks work for a week; purpose works for a career. Know what each athlete plays for — the answer differs, and coaching the individual beats coaching the roster.

title: Teaching tactics
d: Cricket tactics: teach the shape walking before running.
definition: Cricket tactics: teach the shape walking before running.
description: Cricket tactics are taught walking, then jogging, then full speed, then live — skipping steps builds confusion that looks like disobedience. Use freeze-replay: stop the game at the decision moment and ask the player what they saw before telling them. Tactical understanding doubles when athletes scout opponents themselves.

title: Game management
d: Manage Cricket games: know the score, the clock, and your bench.
definition: Manage Cricket games: know the score, the clock, and your bench.
description: Game management in Cricket is clock, score, and personnel: every decision weighs all three. Plan substitution windows and timeout triggers before the game, because pressure destroys improvisation. The best in-game coaches are boring — they execute the plan while opponents panic. Review every game against the plan within 24 hours.

title: Player development
d: Develop Cricket athletes in stages: fundamentals, then position, then leadership.
definition: Develop Cricket athletes in stages: fundamentals, then position, then leadership.
description: Long-term Cricket development runs in stages: broad fundamentals first, positional craft second, leadership and game understanding third. Never sacrifice stage one for short-term wins — the twelve-year-old star built on tricks is the sixteen-year-old who quits. Track development in skills mastered, not trophies lifted.

title: Team culture
d: Culture beats strategy in Cricket: set standards, enforce them equally.
definition: Culture beats strategy in Cricket: set standards, enforce them equally.
description: Cricket team culture is what players do when the coach is not watching. Set three to five non-negotiable standards — punctuality, effort, respect — and enforce them with stars and beginners identically. Culture is built in small moments: the senior who picks up cones, the apology after a bad foul. Protect it fiercely.

title: Season planning
d: Plan the Cricket season: preseason, competition, and recovery blocks.
definition: Plan the Cricket season: preseason, competition, and recovery blocks.
description: Season planning for Cricket: preseason builds fitness and installs systems, the competition phase sharpens and maintains, and the off-season restores. Peak for the events that matter; treat the rest as rehearsal. Schedule lighter weeks before big competitions — tired teams make tired decisions.

title: Working with officials
d: Cricket coaches manage officials with respect: ask, never argue.
definition: Cricket coaches manage officials with respect: ask, never argue.
description: Officials in Cricket respond to respect: captains ask questions, coaches never chase calls. Teach athletes that the call stands and the next play matters more. A coach who berates officials teaches athletes to blame — and loses the close calls that respect might have earned.

facts.officials: two on-field umpires plus third umpire and match referee

title: Safety and welfare
d: Cricket safety: the coach is responsible for every athlete's welfare.
definition: Cricket safety: the coach is responsible for every athlete's welfare.
description: Safety in Cricket is the coach's first duty: safe venues and equipment, proper warm-ups, concussion protocols, and the courage to sit a star who is hurt. Welfare extends beyond the body — watch for burnout, anxiety, and the athlete who has gone quiet. No result justifies harming a young person.

title: Scouting opponents
d: Scout Cricket opponents: tendencies, not just talent.
definition: Scout Cricket opponents: tendencies, not just talent.
description: Scouting Cricket opponents means finding tendencies: what they do under pressure, where their shape breaks, who takes the big moments. Give athletes two or three keys, not twenty — overloaded players play slow. Scout yourself too; your own tendencies are the opponent's scouting report.

title: Developing assistants
d: Great Cricket head coaches build great assistants: delegate real responsibility.
definition: Great Cricket head coaches build great assistants: delegate real responsibility.
description: Assistant coaches in Cricket grow when given real ownership — a unit, a phase of practice, a scouting assignment — not just cones and water. Mentor deliberately: explain your decisions, invite challenge in private, and credit publicly. The program outlasts any one coach only if the next one is being built.

title: Coaching ethics
d: Cricket ethics: the scoreboard never outranks the person.
definition: Cricket ethics: the scoreboard never outranks the person.
description: Coaching ethics in Cricket: never sacrifice an athlete's health, dignity, or future for a result. Play by the rules and the spirit of the rules; recruit honestly; cut players with compassion and clarity. The measure of a coach is not the trophy cabinet but the adults the athletes become.

title: Practice games
d: Conditioned Cricket games teach faster than drills alone.
definition: Conditioned Cricket games teach faster than drills alone.
description: Conditioned games in Cricket — small-sided, with rules that reward the week's theme — transfer skills to matches better than isolated drills. Design the constraint so the desired behavior wins: want switching play? Award double for goals after a switch. Let them play; coach with questions at breaks, not commands during.

title: Working with parents
d: Youth Cricket coaches: recruit the parents as allies, not adversaries.
definition: Youth Cricket coaches: recruit the parents as allies, not adversaries.
description: Parents in youth Cricket need a preseason meeting: your philosophy, playing-time policy, and the 24-hour rule for complaints. Most parent problems come from surprise — communicate early and often. Never discuss another child's playing time, and never let a parent coach from the sideline unchallenged.

title: Talent identification
d: Spot Cricket talent: look for athleticism, attitude, and learning speed.
definition: Spot Cricket talent: look for athleticism, attitude, and learning speed.
description: Talent identification in Cricket weighs physical gifts, coachability, and love of the game over current skill — skills can be taught, attitude rarely changes. Watch how prospects handle failure and whether they improve between viewings. The best predictor of future performance is rate of learning, not present ability.

title: Mental training
d: Train the Cricket mind: routines, self-talk, and pressure practice.
definition: Train the Cricket mind: routines, self-talk, and pressure practice.
description: Mental training in Cricket: teach a pre-performance routine, constructive self-talk, and visualization of successful execution. Simulate pressure in practice — consequences for misses, noise, scoreboard scenarios — so competition feels familiar. Confidence is built from preparation evidence, not pep talks.

title: Integrating fitness
d: Blend fitness into Cricket skill work: fit players learn faster.
definition: Blend fitness into Cricket skill work: fit players learn faster.
description: Fitness integration in Cricket: embed conditioning inside skill drills rather than bolting on separate running — players stay engaged and learn tired, like matches demand. Keep pure fitness blocks short and purposeful. Monitor workload; the fittest team is the one that trains hardest without breaking.

title: Managing injuries
d: Injured Cricket athletes need a plan, honesty, and patience.
definition: Injured Cricket athletes need a plan, honesty, and patience.
description: Injury management in Cricket: follow medical advice exactly, keep the athlete connected to the team, and set criteria-based return milestones — not dates. The re-injury risk peaks in the first month back; progress through controlled contact before full competition. Never let anyone — including the athlete — rush the process.

title: Video review
d: Cricket video: short clips, one fix each, athletes involved.
definition: Cricket video: short clips, one fix each, athletes involved.
description: Video review in Cricket works in 15-minute blocks: three clips maximum, one fix per clip, and athletes analyzing before the coach speaks. Show good examples as often as errors — the brain copies what it sees celebrated. Team sessions build shared understanding; individual clips build personal accountability.

title: Pre-game preparation
d: Cricket pre-game: same routine, clear roles, calm minds.
definition: Cricket pre-game: same routine, clear roles, calm minds.
description: Pre-game preparation in Cricket: a fixed timeline, a dynamic warm-up that ends at game intensity, equipment checks, and two or three tactical keys — no new information. The routine's job is to make the big game feel like every other game. Arrive early enough that nothing is rushed.

title: Post-game review
d: Review Cricket games within 24 hours: facts first, feelings later.
definition: Review Cricket games within 24 hours: facts first, feelings later.
description: Post-game review in Cricket: wait for emotions to cool, then review against the game plan with video — what worked, what broke, one fix for training. Praise effort publicly, correct privately, and never humiliate. The review's product is next week's practice plan, not blame.
